researchQuestion: Can real reviewed translation failures support a paired-source semantic-defect detector/localizer for COBOL and Java?
searchConclusion: Real reviewed compiler regression candidates exist, but no sufficiently sized ready-to-train public corpus of reviewed enterprise COBOL-to-Java defect/fix/source triples was established by this search. This is not a proof that no such corpus exists.

limitations: Output files lack task IDs; pinned ordinal order plus method/class checks does not independently prove identity.
Java benchmark tests are not a direct COBOL oracle.
Shared replay is bounded and partly selected after screening; it is not a model-performance evaluation.
Four disagreeing input cases represent two source-task defect candidates, not four independent defect families.
Existing23reserved families remain unexecuted in this audit, but historical retrieval exposure remains disclosed.

expandedAdjudication.limitation: Post-screening exploratory curation. Multiple witnesses do not increase the number of independent faulty programs; no defect-model accuracy is measured.

nextAdmissionSteps: Pin source, faulty and fixed artifacts with SHA256 plus compiler/runtime versions and flags.
Reproduce failure before the fix and pass after the fix using an unchanged oracle.
Separate compilation/infrastructure failures from behavior mismatches.
Ensure the changed behavior is observable in the model input, including necessary helper/runtime context.
Record independent defect-family/project groups and resolve overlap with HumanEval/EvalPlus/CodeNet and the existing23 reserved task families.
Obtain reliable unaffected controls; a passing finite test suite is not proof of equivalence.
Freeze model selection and thresholds on grouped development data before scoring an independent reviewed COBOL-to-Java defect holdout.
